applies_why: The judge text declares a single verse UNDERDETERMINED based on its admission of two readings, which is the single-verse ambiguity K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed whether 'admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings' means the verse carries two senses at once (so it is not open and both stand) or merely that its words allow two possible constructions (so UNDERDETERMINED could follow).
why: The judge makes the single verse's admitted dual readings the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's command that such a verse is not open and both senses stand.
